papers.abstract: Main duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (MD-IPMN) carries a substantial risk of malignant transformation and often requires surgical resection.1,2 Preservation of the remnant pancreas remains an important goal, particularly in elderly patients.3,4 Therefore, determining the optimal extent of resection requires a careful balance between oncological safety and preservation of pancreatic function.5,6 The utility of intraoperative pancreatoscopy during robotic pancreatoduodenectomy (RPD) for this purpose has not been well established.7 METHODS: We present two elderly patients with MD-IPMN who underwent RPD combined with intraoperative pancreatoscopy. After pancreatic transection, a Spyglass was introduced through a robotic port #1 and advanced into the remnant pancreatic duct under robotic guidance. The main pancreatic duct and branch ducts were systematically inspected for findings suspicious for high-grade dysplasia or skip lesions.8 Frozen-section analysis of the pancreatic margin was performed in both cases. The patients were in their 70s with pancreatic head IPMN and pancreatic duct dilation. Intraoperative pancreatoscopy demonstrated no suspicious lesions within the remnant pancreas. Frozen-section analysis confirmed the absence of carcinoma or high-grade dysplasia at the pancreatic margin. Based on these findings, no additional pancreatic resection was required, and the remnant pancreas was preserved in both patients. Final pathology revealed mixed-type IPMN with high-grade dysplasia and no invasive carcinoma in both cases. Intraoperative pancreatoscopy can be safely integrated into RPD and serves as an adjunct to preoperative imaging, potentially facilitating targeted biopsy. This approach may support preservation of the remnant pancreas in elderly patients with MD-IPMN.

papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by severe immunosuppression and metabolic reprogramming, yet the spatial dynamics of lipid flux between malignant and stromal cells remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a profound, type-specific metabolic rewiring in HCC driven by the widespread downregulation of fatty acid transport protein 5 (FATP5). FATP5 deficiency in malignant cells selectively attenuates the uptake of long-chain fatty acids (LCFAs), creating an extracellular lipid surplus that is passively sequestered by neighboring FATP3-expressing tumor-associated endothelial cells (TECs). Within TECs, accumulated LCFAs function as endogenous ligands that activate the nuclear receptor PPARγ, culminating in the robust transcriptional upregulation and paracrine secretion of the chemokine CXCL12. Endothelial-derived CXCL12 subsequently engages CXCR4 on infiltrating CD8+ T cells, inducing PD-1 expression and driving terminal T-cell exhaustion, thereby establishing an immunosuppressive niche that accelerates tumor progression. Importantly, our data suggest that HCC subtypes marked by FATP5 depletion and CXCL12+ TEC enrichment may possess potential therapeutic susceptibility to PPARγ antagonism or anti-PD-1 immune checkpoint blockade. Besides affecting the secretory function of TECs, accumulated LCFAs can impair endothelial barrier function, thereby creating a microenvironment with hematogenous metastasis risk. Collectively, our findings delineate a novel tumor-promoting microenvironment cascade orchestrated by LCFA spatial redistribution, providing a promising mechanistic foundation to support the future development of targeted precision interventions for FATP5-low HCC.

papers.abstract: Advanced sarcomas remain therapeutically challenging. We evaluated treatment implementation and clinical outcomes after molecular tumor board recommendations. We retrospectively analyzed 125 sarcoma patients discussed in our multidisciplinary Molecular and Familial Tumor Board between 2017 and 2023. Clinical benefit was assessed by treatment implementation and by the ratio of progression-free survival on molecularly guided therapy versus the preceding treatment line (PFS2/PFS1). Overall survival (OS) was measured from first board discussion. A total of 252 pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant records across 133 genes were identified. Molecular profiling enabled therapy recommendations in 71 of 125 patients (56.8%), with treatment implementation in 41 (32.8%). PFS2/PFS1 evaluation was feasible in 29 patients, and nine (31.0%) had a documented ratio > 1.3. Median PFS2 was 102 days (95% CI 63-233). Two of seven patients (28.6%) receiving poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitor-containing regimens had ratios > 1.3. Median OS in 124 patients was 14.6 months (95% CI 11.7-18.5; global log-rank p = 0.220). Molecular tumor board-guided therapy identified treatment options for selected sarcoma patients. Prolonged disease control in individual PARP-treated cases provides a positive signal that warrants prospective evaluation.

papers.abstract: A recent population-based cohort study of Seoul residents in South Korea reported increased incidence of several cancers within one year of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. We examined whether a short-term, population-level change in cancer incidence trends was detectable at the national vaccination rollout, using a design that does not compare vaccinated with unvaccinated individuals. We conducted an interrupted time series analysis of Korea National Health Insurance Service data for 36,024,394 individuals born between 1955 and 2004, covering February 2011 to September 2025 (176 months). The intervention point was August 2021, when cumulative first-dose coverage exceeded 50%. Monthly incidence of 13 cancer categories defined by ICD-10 code ranges and of four site-specific cancers (stomach, colorectum, lung and prostate) was compared with counterfactual forecasts from ARIMA/SARIMA models, and segmented regression estimated immediate level and trend changes (significance threshold P < 0.01). The placement of the intervention point was varied from 0 to 18 months, and the resulting estimates were compared with those obtained at 30 placebo points in the pre-pandemic period. Overall, 89.3% of the population received at least one dose. No immediate level change (relative risk 0.923-1.072) or trend change (0.995-1.005) reached significance for any of the 13 categories, and none reached significance for the four site-specific cancers. Across the lag grid, 2.0% of estimates met the threshold, compared with 4.1% at placebo points. The 99% confidence limits excluded immediate increases larger than 8.9% to 23.0% across the 13 categories and 8.1% to 23.4% across the four site-specific cancers. The national SARS-CoV-2 vaccination rollout in South Korea was not accompanied by a detectable short-term, population-level change in cancer incidence trends over the 50 months that followed. papers.abstract: We examined the associations of parity and breastfeeding with postmenopausal breast density, longitudinal changes in breast density, and breast cancer risk, and assessed the extent to which breast density mediates these relationships. We analyzed a cohort of women who underwent mammography in 2009-2010 and had at least one follow-up mammogram through 2016. Parity and breastfeeding history were self-reported, breast density was classified using Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS), and relative risks (RRs) were estimated using Poisson regression. Mediation analysis evaluated the contributions of baseline breast density and its longitudinal change. Lower parity and shorter breastfeeding duration were associated with higher baseline breast density and less favorable density trajectories over time, including a greater likelihood of increasing density and a lower likelihood of decreasing density. Compared with women with at least two children who breastfed for > 12 months, women with one child who did not breastfeed had a higher breast cancer risk (RR: 1.53; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.43-1.64), with a clear dose-response pattern across parity and breastfeeding categories. Parity showed stronger associations than breastfeeding duration with both breast density and breast cancer risk, and these associations were generally stronger among women aged 65 years or older. Baseline breast density and its longitudinal change mediated approximately 10%-15% of the associations between reproductive factors and breast cancer risk. These findings suggest that reproductive history has long-term effects on breast tissue composition and partly explains subsequent breast cancer risk in postmenopausal women.

papers.abstract: Fifty years ago, Zech et al. in this journal described for the first time the t(8;14) as a recurrent chromosomal aberration in Burkitt lymphoma (BL). Nevertheless, in regions where BL is not endemic, a subset of lymphomas with features of BL lacks the t(8;14)/IG::MYC and instead represents high-grade B-cell lymphoma with 11q aberration (HGBCL,11q). As Zech et al. already noted the cell line BJAB to be an exception as BL from a 5-year Kenyan girl in being EBV-negative, lacking the t(8;14) but showing a chromosome 11 aberration, we here revisited and updated the molecular features of BJAB. Genetic analyses confirmed its East African origin and absence of IG::MYC but unraveled complex 11q aberrations, including gains in 11q14.1-q23.1, loss of 11q23.2qter, and, notably, a nonreciprocal 5'KMT2A::CLTC3'-fusion. The mutational landscape contained genes typically mutated in mature B-cell lymphomas but no driver genes restricted to BL. Therefore, we hypothesize that BJAB derives from an African HGBCL,11q. To investigate the presence of this entity in East Africa, we analyzed 24 cases with Burkitt or high-grade morphology diagnosed at Kenyatta National Hospital. Twenty cases fulfilled the morphological and immunophenotypical criteria for the diagnosis of BLs (11 EBV-positive, 9 EBV-negative). Genetic testing in these cases identified one EBV-negative case (20 years) as MYC-nonrearranged but displaying the typical 11q pattern, thus representing HGBCL,11q. Among the four HGBCL with intermediate features, two showed gains in 11q including the region typically deleted in HGBCL,11q. Our findings establish HGBCL,11q as a relevant differential molecular diagnosis to Burkitt lymphoma in sub-Saharan Africa.

papers.abstract: Seminal extracellular vesicles (EVs) hold promise as a source of biomarkers for urogenital cancers. In this study, small seminal EVs were isolated from healthy donors by size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) and three ultracentrifugation (UC) protocols, with or without filtration. EV samples prepared by UC had a higher abundance of typical EV-related molecules such as CD9, CD81, and Alix, compared to SEC preparations. However, ribosomal and ER-related proteins were more enriched in SEC samples. Furthermore, the level of several nonvesicular proteins and/or EV-corona proteins was higher in SEC samples. The addition of a filtration step in the UC protocols also reduced the abundance of these proteins. Finally, we found that the isolation protocol affected the presence of prostate cancer-specific proteins in the EV samples, with membrane proteins such as FOLH1, TMPRSS2, and PSCA enriched in samples prepared by UC. In conclusion, our results suggest that SEC and UC enrich for different EV populations, which should be considered when analyzing cancer biomarkers. Moreover, UC samples contained fewer nonvesicular proteins and/or EV-corona proteins, which may enable a more precise detection of EV-based cancer biomarkers.

papers.abstract: Gynaecological malignancies account for over 1.4 million new diagnoses, with outcomes constrained by late-stage presentation and chemoresistance. Dysregulated redox homeostasis is a hallmark of tumourigenesis. Tumour cells maintain elevated basal reactive oxygen species (ROS), which support proliferative signalling but may also increase susceptibility to further oxidative stress. Vitamin D, acting through the vitamin D receptor (VDR), has antiproliferative and pro-apoptotic effects across cancer models, but its ability to amplify ROS beyond an apoptotic threshold in gynaecological malignancies remains unresolved. We conducted a narrative literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, ClinicalTrials.gov and the Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results databases, using terms related to vitamin D and its metabolites, ROS/oxidative stress, apoptosis and gynaecological malignancies. Preclinical evidence indicates that calcitriol and related compounds can induce ROS-mediated mitochondrial apoptosis, modulate autophagy and arrest the cell cycle. In ovarian cancer, non-HGSOC cell data suggest that mutant TP53 may alter calcitriol responses, requiring validation in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma models. In cervical cancer, calcitriol radiosensitises human papillomavirus-positive cell lines through autophagy suppression, whilst an in vivo calcitriol-cisplatin study reported improved survival. In endometrial cancer, thioredoxin-interacting protein induction is a candidate mechanism for selective ROS-mediated apoptosis, although this remains context-dependent. Clinical evidence is heterogeneous: higher 25-hydroxyvitamin D status has shown modest inverse associations with ovarian cancer mortality; small trials report regression or reduced recurrence of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia; no randomised controlled trial evidence supports efficacy in invasive cervical cancer; and associations with endometrial cancer incidence are largely null. Current evidence does not support vitamin D supplementation as an oncology-specific intervention. Future research should prioritise biomarker-stratified trials incorporating VDR genotype, CYP24A1 profiling, pre-specified 25(OH)D targets and pharmacokinetically informed dosing.

papers.abstract: Radiotherapy is often limited by tumor-intrinsic DNA repair and an immunosuppressive microenvironment, both of which are reinforced by lactate accumulation. Here, we develop a CXCR4-engineered enucleated hepatocyte cytoplast platform decorated with Au-Pt Janus nanorobots (AP/LCCXCR4) to deplete intratumoral lactate and amplify radiation-induced oxidative stress. The hepatocyte cytoplasts home to tumors and consume lactate through gluconeogenesis, reducing repair-associated protein lactylation and impairing MRE11-RAD50-NBS1 (MRN) co-fractionation and chromatin recruitment, thereby impairing double-strand break repair. In parallel, the Au-Pt nanorobots enhance reactive oxygen species generation under acidic tumor conditions, increasing radiation damage. In radioresistant colorectal cancer models and a metastatic cervical cancer model, AP/LCCXCR4 combined with radiotherapy sustains DNA damage, promotes immunogenic cell death, reduces immunosuppressive myeloid and regulatory T (Treg) cell populations, enhances dendritic cell maturation and CD8+ T cell activation, and improves tumor control and survival.

papers.abstract: Inflammatory transcriptional responses mediated by NF-κB are diverse despite similar upstream activation signals. Because phosphorylation of the NF-κB subunit RelA/p65 promotes interaction with co-activators CREB-binding protein/E1A binding protein p300 (CBP/p300) and selectively affects gene expression, we asked whether this modification distinguishes regulatory architectures underlying distinct immune functions. In macrophages carrying a Rela Ser276Ala mutation, p65 phosphorylation at serine 276 (S276) was dispensable for NF-κB binding to primed enhancers but essential for recruitment to nucleosome-occluded regions lacking pre-bound transcription factors (TFs) and activating histone marks. Such latent enhancers required phosphorylated NF-κB to recruit CBP/p300, promote histone acetylation, and open chromatin. Genes linked to these enhancers, including inflammatory mediators, were selectively impaired in S276A macrophages. Although antiviral responses remained intact, Rela Ser276Ala mice resisted endotoxin shock but were susceptible to bacterial infection. Thus, NF-κB responses are functionally partitioned by enhancer architecture: phosphorylation-sensitive sites define a latent enhancer compartment with NF-κB-dominated regulatory architecture, whereas primed sites are embedded in broader networks of lineage-determining and inducible TFs, yielding distinct biological outputs.

papers.abstract: Physical activity promotes health primarily by decelerating the aging process. Bone is one of the tissues capable of sensing mechanical force and can adapt to different physical demands. However, its role in whole-body aging is unknown. We found that reduced mechano-sensing in osteocytes, caused by deletion of the mechanosensory channel, Piezo1, accelerated whole-body aging in mice. Dynamic tibial axial loading (DTAL) in mice at 20-24 months of age extended both healthspan and lifespan (9.4%/79.5 days). Furthermore, DTAL reversed bone marrow immunosenescence and induced anti-aging and protective factors while downregulating pro-aging and pro-inflammatory factors. We also identified pigment epithelium-derived factor (PEDF) as a novel mechano-responsive anti-aging factor that is highly associated with healthy aging in humans. Thus, our findings highlighted an essential role for bone mechano-sensing in whole-body aging. This could potentially be manipulated to prevent aging, extend health, and aid those unable to exercise or with decreased mobility.

papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) and its progression to chronic kidney disease (CKD) remain major unmet clinical challenges for which effective therapies are lacking. Although sensory neurons are recognized as key regulators of tissue injury and repair via neuroimmune crosstalk, their organization and function within the kidney are poorly understood. Here, we delineate a renal neuroimmune axis in which nociceptive neurons protect against ischemia-reperfusion (I/R)-induced kidney injury. Using whole-organ tissue clearing and three-dimensional imaging, we mapped an extensive network of nociceptive sensory fibers throughout the renal parenchyma. Ablation of TRPV1+ nociceptors aggravated renal dysfunction, tubular necrosis, and fibrosis after I/R, whereas chemogenetic activation conferred protection. Mechanistically, the sensory neuropeptide calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), which is upregulated after injury, acts via the CALCRL-RAMP1 receptor complex on monocytes/macrophages, engaging the cAMP-PKA pathway to suppress pro-inflammatory cytokine and chemokine expression, thereby limiting myeloid infiltration and tubular injury. Importantly, we also found reduced renal CGRP abundance in kidneys from individuals with diabetes and older adults, who are at high risk for AKI and CKD, as well as in corresponding mouse models. In these vulnerable settings, exogenous CGRP more effectively reduced I/R-induced kidney injury. Our findings establish a dorsal root ganglia-kidney neuroimmune circuit that restrains I/R-induced renal inflammation and identify CGRP signaling as a potential therapeutic target to mitigate AKI and its progression to CKD, particularly in high-risk diabetic and elderly populations.

papers.abstract: Transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) are widely used to identify genes involved in complex traits and to infer the direction of gene effects on traits. However, despite their popularity, it remains unclear how accurately TWAS recover the true direction of a gene's effect on a trait. Here we estimate the false sign rate of TWAS for plasma proteins, leveraging the expectation that increased gene expression should generally increase protein expression. We then extend this framework to complex traits, where loss-of-function burden tests provide the expected direction of effect. In both analyses, we observe high discordance with expectations, with TWAS showing a false sign rate of 23% for plasma proteins and 33% for complex traits. We propose that much of the sign discordance arises when expression quantitative trait loci in non-trait-relevant tissues tag haplotypes associated with traits in genome-wide association studies via distinct, tightly linked regulatory variants, yielding spurious TWAS associations with the correct genes but with unreliable direction of effect. These findings show that TWAS-based direction-of-effect estimates should be interpreted with caution and raise concerns about the reliability of TWAS more broadly.

papers.abstract: Wild emmer wheat (Triticum turgidum ssp. dicoccoides, BBAA), the wild progenitor of cultivated tetraploid and hexaploid wheats, provides an important reference for investigating centromere reorganization during polyploidization and domestication. Here we generated a near-complete genome assembly of wild emmer wheat, including centromeric regions for all 14 centromeres. Comparative analyses with cultivated tetraploid and hexaploid wheats revealed extensive variation in centromere-associated sequences and centromere-proximal structure, as well as distinct subgenome-associated patterns in the A and B subgenomes. The A subgenome was characterized by positional shifts and sequence turnover of CRW-rich centromere-derived blocks, whereas the B subgenome showed reduced CentT566 satellite abundance accompanied by localized retention or expansion on specific chromosomes. These results provide a high-resolution tetraploid wheat reference and reveal subgenome-associated patterns of centromere remodeling during wheat polyploid evolution.

papers.abstract: Current vaccine adjuvants, such as aluminum salts and emulsions, are limited by weak induction of cytotoxic T cell immunity and restricted ability to promote T helper type 1 responses, highlighting the need for safer and more effective alternatives. Here we show that microparticles generated from erythrocytes by controlled ultraviolet irradiation function as potent T helper type 1-skewing adjuvants that enhance tumour antigen-specific cytotoxic T cell responses in vitro and in multiple mouse tumour models. Following uptake by dendritic cells, these microparticles traffic to lysosomes and deliver haem cargo that is subsequently transported to the nucleus. Mechanistically, the particles elevate lysosomal pH, promoting lysosome movement towards the nucleus and enabling haem transfer, where haem activates REV-ERB⍺ and forms a co-repressor complex that suppresses peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma, thereby relieving inhibition of dendritic cell maturation and antigen presentation. In vaccination settings, combining tumour antigens with erythrocyte-derived microparticles enhances cytotoxic T cell activation and suppresses tumour growth with minimal toxicity. These findings establish host-derived vesicles as a promising platform for next-generation cancer vaccine adjuvants.

papers.abstract: Local activation of regulatory T (Treg) cells represents a promising strategy for wound repair and tissue regeneration. However, current Treg-based therapies rely on adoptive cell transfer, which requires ex vivo expansion and reinfusion, posing challenges to donor variability and tissue specificity. Here we engineer a hydrogel-based system for in situ Treg activation at injury sites through the controlled release of AS2863619 (AS), a cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor. AS is incorporated into collagen hydrogels at concentrations exceeding its solubility limit, reducing burst release and extending the release half-life. This continuous exposure to Treg-inducing agents stabilizes Foxp3 expression in CD4+ T cells, thereby enabling Treg induction and stabilization. The incorporation of laponite nanoparticles further slows AS release and prolongs drug retention. In a calvarial bone-defect model, AS-loaded hydrogels induce dose-dependent Treg cell activation, reduce pro-inflammatory macrophage responses and enhance bone regeneration. Notably, AS-laponite hydrogels achieve complete defect bridging in some cases. By providing spatiotemporal control over Treg populations without the need for cell isolation and expansion, this approach offers a scalable alternative for immunomodulation and tissue repair.

papers.abstract: Improving outcomes for high-risk acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) patients requires increasingly personalized treatment strategies that leverage molecular and omics-based assays as well as functional screens. However, to date, only a few of these approaches are clinically actionable and easily adopted in clinical settings. To that end, we report a combination drug screening assay (GradientScreen) that correlates with clinical outcomes using standard paediatric ALL treatment protocols. This assay uses a microfluidic device to generate overlapping drug gradients and implements an analysis framework that characterizes drug synergy and efficacy in a ratiometric manner. Using partial least squares regression, we show that our combination response metrics correlate with both minimal residual disease (MRD) following initiation of treatment and later clinical end-points. Here, we further demonstrate that this system could be used to evaluate response to experimental therapeutic regimens in patients who did not respond to standard treatment. This assay can serve as a research-enabling tool for the field, with potential to integrate into clinical pathology workflows to identify difficult-to-treat ALL patients and screen for alternative treatment strategies at diagnosis.

papers.abstract: Cytokines are critical regulators of central nervous system (CNS) integrity, acting not only as immune messengers but also as signals that coordinate interactions among glial and neuronal cells, resident macrophages, such as microglia and border-associated macrophages, and infiltrating leukocytes. These circuits establish basal immune tone, shape responses to perturbation, and promote tissue adaptation and recovery. In this Review, we examine selected cytokine pathways across homeostasis, inflammatory or degenerative tissue damage and repair to develop a framework for how cytokine networks preserve, destabilize and restore CNS integrity. We focus on CSF-1, IL-34, TGFβ and IL-33 in homeostasis; IL-1, TNF, GM-CSF and IFNγ in inflammation; type I and II interferons in antiviral and neurodegenerative states; and IL-12 at the interface of innate sensing, adaptive immunity and tissue-protective adaptation. By focusing on instructive modules, we highlight broader organizing principles and how cytokine miscalibration can lead to neurological disease across diverse contexts.

papers.abstract: DNA's anti-parallel structure presents a topological challenge to the replisome, as leading and lagging strands must be synthesized in opposite directions. How lagging-strand synthesis is coordinated with leading-strand synthesis remains unresolved in eukaryotes. To address this question, we directly visualized the dynamics of lagging-strand polymerases Pol α and Pol δ at active replication forks using single-molecule imaging in Xenopus nuclear extracts. Surprisingly, we find that neither Pol α nor Pol δ is stably tethered to the replisome. Instead, lagging-strand synthesis occurs distributively and entails the rapid recruitment of new molecules of Pol α and Pol δ for each Okazaki fragment. Consequently, leading- and lagging-strand synthesis are not intrinsically coupled. We propose that metazoans solve the problem of anti-parallel replication not by actively coordinating leading- and lagging-strand synthesis, but instead simply by recruiting new polymerases to synthesize each Okazaki fragment.

papers.abstract: People who become pregnant after living kidney donation may be at increased risk of pregnancy-related adverse outcomes, although the evidence is unclear. To determine whether pregnancies after living kidney donation are associated with a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes than matched pregnancies among nondonors. This matched cohort study used provincial administrative health care databases from Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta, Canada, and included living female kidney donors aged 18 to 42 years who donated a kidney between July 1992 and August 2021 and subsequently had singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation. These pregnancies were matched 1:4 with singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation among female nondonors. Pregnancies in donors and nondonors were matched on delivery date, age at delivery, years between cohort entry and delivery, number of prior pregnancies, and income. Final follow-up occurred until March 2023. Outcome analysis occurred from August 2024 to September 2026. The primary outcome was a composite of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia. Secondary outcomes included 12 maternal, fetal and neonatal adverse outcomes, including the individual components of the primary outcome, the composite of low birth weight or preterm birth, and small for gestational age at birth. The sample included 385 pregnancies in 252 living kidney donors (mean [SD] age, 27.8 [5.0] years) matched to 1540 pregnancies in 1535 nondonors (mean [SD] age, 27.0 [4.8] years). The primary composite outcome of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia occurred in 46 donor pregnancies (11.9%) and 128 nondonor pregnancies (8.3%; risk ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.10-2.08). Among the 12 secondary outcomes, the 95% CI for the risk ratio excluded 1.00 for the outcome of small for gestational age, which occurred in 53 donor pregnancies (13.8%) and 121 nondonor pregnancies (7.9%) (risk ratio, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.37-2.52). In this study, pregnancy after living kidney donation was associated with a higher risk of the composite outcome of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia, when compared with matched pregnancies in nondonors. Most postdonation pregnancies were uncomplicated. These findings support counseling donor candidates who may become pregnant about this risk and informing the prenatal care of donors who become pregnant.

papers.abstract: Cellular heterogeneity and plasticity are hallmarks of cancer that contribute to tumor growth and therapy resistance. Here, we investigated metabolic heterogeneity in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), an aggressive cancer type with considerable plasticity between neuroendocrine (NE) and non-NE cellular states. Through integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses, we identified a universal dependency on exogenous cysteine/cystine (Cys) across all NE/non-NE SCLC cell states. Notably, NE and non-NE cells with low ASCL1 transcription factor levels underwent ferroptosis upon Cys depletion, whereas ASCL1high cells underwent apoptosis while remaining resistant to ferroptosis. This ferroptosis resistance was driven by the direct transcriptional activation of GCH1 by ASCL1, resulting in increased levels of the antioxidants BH4/BH2. Accordingly, combined Cys depletion and inhibition of BH4/BH2 synthesis reduced tumor growth in patient-derived xenografts. These findings demonstrate that metabolic state influences cell-death susceptibility in SCLC and provide a rationale for therapeutic strategies that exploit these metabolic differences.

papers.abstract: Whether a decline in taurine drives aging is debated, and despite high millimolar intracellular concentrations, its function as a potential guardian of cytosolic homeostasis is unclear. Here, we show that aging increases circulating taurine concentrations in humans and mice. Further elevating taurine in aged mice enhances health span, engaging anti-inflammatory pathways previously linked to youthfulness, and reduces mortality from sepsis and inflammasome-mediated inflammation, suggesting an enantiostatic response. Mechanistically, diverse NLRP3-specific "danger signals" induce taurine efflux from macrophages as a proximal step to activate the inflammasome and the resultant pyroptosis. Taurine restoration in macrophages prevents NLRP3-induced trans-Golgi network disassembly, thereby suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Conversely, lowering taurine biosynthesis combined with reduced bioavailability in macrophages exacerbated inflammasome activation. In humans, sustained caloric restriction elevates adipose tissue taurine and is accompanied by lower inflammation. Together, we identify taurine as an immunometabolic rheostat that links danger sensing to NLRP3 inflammasome activation, suggesting taurine-based strategies to alleviate inflammaging and inflammasomopathies.

papers.abstract: Cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and natural killer cells are critical effectors of anti-tumor immunity. Cytotoxic lymphocytes eliminate tumor cells by releasing perforin (Prf1), a pore-forming protein that enables granzymes (Gzms) to enter target cells and trigger both caspase-dependent and -independent cell death. Here, we uncover a previously unrecognized, Gzm-independent function of Prf1. We find that Prf1 directly induces tumoral ferroptosis, an iron- and lipid-dependent form of cell death. Mechanistically, Prf1-mediated pore formation drives endocytosis of the transferrin receptor, which increases cellular iron uptake. Prf1 promotes the formation of endosomal-mitochondrial contacts, which leads to mitochondrial iron accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and tumor cell ferroptosis. Dietary iron supplementation suppresses tumor progression in murine tumor models in a Prf1-dependent manner. Higher Prf1 expression correlates with improved survival and enhanced response to immune checkpoint blockade in patients with cancer. These findings define a Gzm-independent function of Prf1 as a direct executioner of cancer cell death through ferroptosis.

papers.abstract: The environment in which a glacier terminates can strongly influence its behaviour, stability and future evolution, yet the relationship between terminus type and glacier dynamics at the global scale remains poorly constrained. Here we present a globally-complete classification of glacier termini distinguishing between land, lake, marine and shelf environments, and integrate it with datasets of glacier geometry, dynamics and climate. We show that although lake-, marine- and shelf-terminating glaciers comprise only 3.2% of glaciers globally, they account for over half of global glacier area and mass loss. We also show that lake- and marine-terminating glaciers flow, on average, 10% and 44% faster than land-terminating glaciers, respectively. Furthermore, specific (area-normalised) mass loss rates at lake-terminating glaciers are 57% greater than those at land- and marine-terminating glaciers. Our findings underscore the need for improved representation of non-land glacier termini in models of glacier evolution and sea-level rise, and suggest that distinguishing the environmental and geometric controls of termini on glacier dynamics remains an important challenge for future research.

papers.abstract: Van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures allow the engineering of magnetic and electronic properties via interfacial orbital hybridization and charge transfer. The resulting electric fields can give rise to Rashba spin-orbit coupling and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, which may stabilize novel two-dimensional magnetic phases. While such emergent magnetic 'interphases' may offer a promising platform for spin-based electronics, direct spectroscopic evidence for them is still lacking. Here, we report electric-field tunable Zeeman effects with Landé g-factors up to ≈ 230 at the interface of graphene and the vdW ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2. They arise from an interplay of local-moment canting and the itinerant orbital moments of Fe3GeTe2, producing a giant asymmetric level splitting. Exploiting the inelastic phonon gap of graphene, scanning tunneling spectroscopy allows us to access the buried interface properties, and quantify Faraday-like screening. Our findings provide new insights and opportunities for electrically controlled interface magnetism, e.g. for spintronics and orbitronics devices.

papers.abstract: Global oceans store large quantities of human-made persistent hydrophobic organic contaminants (HOCs), driven by the organic carbon (OC) cycle. Despite diverse organic matter composition, bulk OC is typically treated as a uniform sorbent when assessing HOC fate. Significant uncertainty remains regarding the factors controlling variability in the sorption of HOCs by organic matter. Using surface sediments across the Eurasian Arctic shelves, spanning a land-to-ocean continuum of OC, we show that polychlorinated biphenyl concentrations per unit marine‑derived OC are up to an order of magnitude higher than those per unit terrestrial OC. Coupling these empirical relationships with a state‑of‑the‑art ocean biogeochemistry model shows that climate‑driven increases in marine primary production in the Eurasian Arctic shelves lead to 1.3 times more HOC removal from the water column. These findings reveal that both OC quantity and quality control the sediment HOC sink and that climate‑induced shifts in OC cycles may restructure HOC fate in the Arctic Ocean.

papers.abstract: Uranocene, [UIV(η8-C8H8)2], is the actinide equivalent to ferrocene. While ferrocene is readily oxidised to the ferrocenium cation, higher oxidation states of uranocene are unknown. Here we report the elusive uranocenium cation, [UV(η8-C8H8)2]+, and demonstrate using electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy and magnetometry that this formal U(V) complex has a 5 f 1 ground state. Enhanced uranium 5 f and 6 d mixing into filled δ-symmetry bonding orbitals in uranocenium, compared to uranocene, amplifies interorbital electron-electron repulsion, and counteracts bond length contraction, which minimises structural change. This manifests in solution where the uranocene/uranocenium redox couple exhibits near-ideal electrochemical reversibility, and in the solid-state where X-ray diffraction studies show minimal U-C bond length change upon oxidation. This demonstrates a case where actinide covalency governs molecular structure and physical properties across both solid and solution phases.

papers.abstract: Fast qubit control is essential for scalable quantum computing. However, the strong driving that is required can induce significant leakage from the computational subspace, particularly in weakly anharmonic qubits. We demonstrate single qubit gates with a total leakage error consistently below 2.0 × 10-5 on a transmon qubit, and obtain fidelities above 99.98% at 6.8 ns pulse duration in both X and X/2 gates. This is achieved by removing direct transitions beyond nearest-neighbor levels using double recursive applications of Derivative Removal by Adiabatic Gate pulse shape. We also introduce the amplified leakage error sequence which can directly measure the leakage error down to 10-6. We test single qubit gates across a range of pulse durations using multiple benchmarking methods to reveal the error channels. The presented approach can be straightforwardly adapted by other platforms.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by a dense desmoplastic stroma and early metastatic dissemination, both of which contribute to its poor prognosis. While forkhead box protein 3 (FOXP3) is best known as a lineage-defining transcription factor in regulatory T cells (Tregs), its aberrant expression in cancer cell-specific FOXP3 (c-FOXP3) may also support tumor-cell-intrinsic progression. Our findings suggest that high c-FOXP3 expression is closely linked to aggressive disease behavior and metastatic progression in PDAC. c-FOXP3 enhanced migration, invasion within three-dimensional collagen-rich matrices, and dissemination in orthotopic models. Integrated transcriptomic analysis, chromatin immunoprecipitation, and wild-type versus binding-site-mutant promoter assays identified matrix metalloproteinase 19 (MMP19) as a direct transcriptional target of c-FOXP3. MMP19 silencing significantly attenuated c-FOXP3-driven migration, matrix invasion, and metastasis. Single-cell sequencing further showed that MMP19 is abundant in cancer-associated fibroblasts but also defines a distinct epithelial pool that is reduced after epithelial Foxp3 deletion. Pharmacological profiling did not identify a validated MMP19-selective inhibitor, whereas the FOXP3-targeting antisense oligonucleotide AZD8701 reduced FOXP3 together with MMP19 mRNA and was accompanied by lower PDAC-cell migration and invasion in vitro. Together, these findings extend the known functions of FOXP3 beyond its classical role in immune tolerance and define a tumor-cell-intrinsic c-FOXP3-MMP19 program that supports matrix-invasive behavior in PDAC and provide preliminary evidence that c-FOXP3 is pharmacologically accessible.

papers.abstract: Cell segmentation is a critical yet under-standardized step in spatial transcriptomics, directly affecting cell identity assignment, spatial organization and downstream biological interpretation. Despite rapid advances in spatial transcriptomics technologies, systematic evaluations of segmentation methods across platforms and biological contexts remain limited. Here we benchmark 11 image-based, transcriptomics-based and multimodal segmentation methods across 15 datasets generated by 5 spatial transcriptomics technologies, spanning 12 human and mouse tissue types. We introduce biologically informed evaluation metrics that quantify segmentation quality, transcript recovery, cell composition, morphology, expression purity and spatial organization. Benchmarking reveals substantial variation in performance across datasets, technologies and evaluation criteria, highlighting trade-offs among segmentation completeness, transcriptomic fidelity and biological interpretability. Cross-technology analyses further demonstrate that segmentation choice critically shapes downstream analyses, including cell-type specificity, transcript contamination and ligand-receptor inference. Together, our unified Nextflow pipeline provides a scalable foundation for standardized evaluation of segmentation and method selection in spatial transcriptomics.

papers.abstract: Mechanochemistry uses mechanical forces to drive chemical transformations, offering an energy-efficient alternative to traditional thermal, optical, or electrical reaction pathways. At the single-molecule scale, controlling structural changes with mechanical stimuli is fundamental for developing nanoscale devices and understanding chemical reactivity. In conventional single-molecule reactions driven by light or electrical currents, energy is supplied through one-way excitation processes, requiring the single-event energy input to exceed the activation energy barrier. Here we show that mechanically driven single-molecule reactions can bypass this limitation, proceeding with a net energy cost below the activation energy. By using atomic force microscopy to induce the structural inversion of individual, bowl-shaped sumanene molecules on a gold surface, we measure the mechanical energy spent during the transformation. The net energy cost is significantly lower than the theoretical activation energy. This sub-barrier reaction occurs because attractive van der Waals forces from the mesoscopic tip body stabilize the transition state more effectively than the final state. Our findings demonstrate a distinct energetic mechanism in mechanochemistry, highlighting alternative strategies for energy-efficient molecular manipulation.

papers.abstract: Severe immune-related adverse events (irAE) in cancer patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) require treatment interruption and immunosuppression. Based on prior preclinical data, in this prospective, single arm, non-randomized phase-Ib/II clinical trial we test the activity of Extracorporeal Photopheresis (ECP) against steroid-refractory irAEs in 30 patients (EudraCT-No.:2021-002073-26). The primary endpoint is the evaluation of the safety of ECP treatment for patients with ICI-induced irAEs. The study meets its pre-specified primary endpoint of less than 50% of patients developing ECP-related severe adverse events (SAE). No ECP-related SAE is observed and ECP-related AEs are reported in 20% (6/30) of patients. Overall response rate for all irAEs is 96.3% (CI 81.0-99.91). Colitis-, hepatitis- and dermatitis-specific response rates are 100% (13/13), 86.7% (13/15) and 100% (3/3), respectively. Secondary endpoints include the assessment of response rate of irAE and overall survival. ECP therapy is associated with reduced granzyme-A/B/K, T-bet, interferon-γ and TNF in peripheral T cells and pro-inflammatory gene-expression in the intestinal tract. The 12-month overall survival rate is 84.3% (CI 63.4%-93.8%). Response correlates with a decrease in inflammatory gene expression in the intestinal tract. These results suggest that ECP is a safe treatment option for SR-irAEs and warrant further investigation in subsequent randomized clinical trials.

papers.abstract: Invikafusp alfa (invika), a first-in-class, bispecific, dual T cell agonistic antibody selectively targeting Vβ6/Vβ10 T cell subsets, is being evaluated in START-001, a multicenter phase 1/2 monotherapy trial in participants with mostly immune checkpoint blockade (ICB)-resistant, antigen-rich solid tumors. Primary outcomes were safety/tolerability and recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) in phase 1 and anti-tumor activity in phase 2. As of 12 March 2025, phase 1 completed dose escalation (n = 34) through dose levels of 0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.08, 0.12 and 0.16 mg kg-1 without reaching maximum tolerated dose, and initial phase 2 enrolled 18 participants. Two participants experienced reversible dose-limiting toxicities, one at each of the 0.08 mg kg-1 and 0.16 mg kg-1 dose levels. The most common treatment-related adverse event was cytokine release syndrome, mainly grades 1 and 2. No treatment-related deaths or non-laboratory grade 4 adverse events were reported. At the optimal biological doses (OBDs; 0.08 mg kg-1 and 0.12 mg kg-1) in combined phase 1 and phase 2 cohorts, the overall objective response rate was 14.8% (4/27), including confirmed partial responses in immunologically cold tumors, such as microsatellite stable colorectal cancer and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative non-small cell lung cancer. No objective responses were seen at doses lower than 0.08 mg kg-1. Invika selectively and potently expanded peripheral and intratumoral Vβ6/Vβ10 T cells, of a predominantly memory-like phenotype, dose-dependently, peaking at the OBDs. Pharmacodynamic increases in interferon-γ and soluble CD25 followed a similar pattern. Integrated analyses from safety, pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic and preliminary anti-tumor data supported the selection of 0.08 mg kg-1 as the RP2D. In conclusion, phase 1 of START-001 met its primary outcomes by demonstrating the acceptable safety profile of invika consistent with its mechanism of action and selecting an RP2D. Initial phase 2 results further corroborated the safety of invika and expanded its preliminary evidence of clinically meaningful anti-tumor activity in ICB-resistant solid tumors, supporting further evaluation in the ongoing phase 2. papers.abstract: Camupepimut (ELI-002 7P) drives mutated KRAS (mKRAS)-specific T cell responses that correlated with disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) in patients with mKRAS pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) in the phase 1 AMPLIFY-201 trial. In the phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial, patients with stage I-III KRAS-mutated PDAC without recurrence within 6 months of standard therapy were randomized 2:1 to camupepimut (n = 96) or standard-of-care/observation (n = 48). Stratification balanced nodal status. The primary DFS endpoint was not met (median 23.8 versus 21.2 months; HR 0.85, P = 0.5329). However, prespecified and exploratory analyses were informative. A numerical DFS advantage at 6 months of 14.0% (75.7% versus 61.7%; HR 0.55, P = 0.0557) corresponded to camupepimut dosing. Post hoc multivariate Cox regression analysis of DFS indicated an improved outcome for camupepimut (adjusted HR 0.47, P = 0.0086), a worse outcome for stage III disease (adjusted HR 2.29, P = 0.0127), an elevated baseline CA19-9 (adjusted HR 3.16, P 9.17-fold over baseline (82.2%, 74/90) correlated with improved DFS (HR 0.22, P < 0.0001), with the median DFS not reached versus 6.08 months for above and below 9.17-fold, respectively. Camupepimut safety was similar to observation, with grade ≥3 adverse events in 10.4% (10/96) versus 14.6% (7/48), and few serious AEs (6.3%, 6/96 versus 8.3%, 4/48; reflecting progression/surgical complication). These efficacy and immunogenicity signals will inform a refined strategy for a confirmatory phase 3 trial. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05726864 .

papers.abstract: In patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) treated with chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy, factors associated with efficacy overlap with prognostic biomarkers. Currently, there is no consensus on optimal product characteristics. We analyzed the phenotypic attributes of the anti-CD19 CAR T therapy axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel) from 580 patients with NHL across multiple clinical trials with long-term follow-up (median, 41.9 months). A high proportion of naive-like (CCR7+CD45RA+) T cells was the most significant feature associated with prolonged progression-free survival (PFS; hazard ratio = 0.46, 95% confidence interval: 0.31-0.68, P = 9.8 × 10-5, high versus low naive-like T cell groups) without impacting safety. The relationship between naive-like T cells and efficacy was independent of tumor microenvironment characteristics (assessed in 112 patients). In multivariate models, the naive-like phenotype outperformed clinicopathologic features such as inflammatory markers and tumor burden, remaining significant after adjusting for product expansion. An inverse correlation was observed between prior lines of therapy and the proportion of naive-like T cells in both product and matched apheresis samples, suggesting a benefit of earlier intervention. The key findings were validated in an independent cohort of 203 patients treated with axi-cel-based therapy or brexucabtagene autoleucel. Mass cytometry by time-of-flight analysis of products from a subgroup of 116 patients confirmed an association between a CD8 naive-like T cell phenotype lacking expression of exhaustion markers, such as TIGIT, LAG-3 and PD-1, and PFS. The evidence generated by this study has the potential to advance the development of more effective cellular therapies.

papers.abstract: Blood phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) accurately detects Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology but is also elevated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), likely reflecting peripheral (big) tau released from muscle. Assays selectively measuring brain-derived (BD-) tau and BD-p-tau217 are therefore needed. We analysed serum BD-tau and p-tau217 in ALS (n = 139), AD (n = 101) and controls (n = 75) using direct immunoassays and after BD-Tau immunoprecipitation (BD-Tau-IP), and tau species in brain (n = 16), spinal cord (n = 11) and muscle (n = 10) by targeted mass spectrometry. With the direct immunoassays, BD-tau and p-tau217 were increased in AD and ALS versus controls. After BD-Tau-IP, BD-tau and BD-p-tau217 were elevated in AD only, improving diagnostic accuracy. Mass spectrometry revealed a central-to-peripheral shift from BD-tau to big tau predominance, with exclusively big p-tau217 detected in muscle. Selective detection of BD-tau species improves the specificity of blood AD biomarkers by reducing peripheral tau confounding.

papers.abstract: Multi-Tb/s optical interconnects for artificial intelligence data centers necessitate high-speed, energy-efficient, and compact transceivers. However, conventional silicon Mach-Zehnder modulators are fundamentally limited by low modulation efficiency and large physical dimensions that typically extend several millimeters, requiring high-swing drivers and power-intensive digital signal processing to achieve data rates exceeding 100 Gb/s per lane. Here we show a silicon photonic crystal waveguide slow-light modulator that overcomes the bandwidth-efficiency trade-off via a built-in electro-optic equalizer. By monolithically integrating optical delay lines and crossings within segmented slow-light phase shifters, we synthesized an on-chip feedforward response that extends the 3-dB bandwidth. The fabricated modulator with a small device length of 320 µm demonstrated 140-Gb/s on-off keying operation with an energy consumption of 26 fJ/bit using drive voltages compatible with fin field-effect transistor-based complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technology. Furthermore, four-level pulse amplitude modulation achieved 180 Gb/s without digital signal processing and 200 Gb/s with a low-complexity 11-tap digital equalizer. By reducing reliance on power-dissipating electronics, this strategy provides a potential route toward future dense multi-Tb/s co-packaged optics for energy-constrained switching systems.

papers.abstract: Highly compliant deformable soft actuators enable the engineering of adaptive life-like systems. Biohybrid living materials expand possibilities for autonomous, self-powered, environmentally responsive systems with easy biological integration. Here, we present a light-driven living soft actuator that integrates the photosynthetic microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii with a pH-responsive poly(3-(acrylamido)phenylboronic acid-acrylamide)/polyacrylamide bilayer hydrogel. When exposed to light, through photosynthesis and N-assimilation, the microalgae locally ionize the polymer network, causing the bilayer actuator to bend. In darkness, through respiration, the microalgae locally release CO2 that protonates the polymer chains, reversing the deformation. This algae actuator enables finely controlled and reversible motions, with a large bending amplitude achieved within 18 hours and an initial response time of 10-20 s, which is maintained over 10 cycles of continuous operation. We demonstrate light-controlled grippers, highlighting the potential of algae-powered actuation for sustainable and autonomous soft devices.

papers.abstract: X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) is essential for extraembryonic tissue growth and embryo development in mice. However, species-specific differences in its timing and regulation have left its role in human development unclear. Here, we show that the in vitro differentiation of naive human pluripotent stem cells to trophoblast stem cells and extraembryonic mesoderm cells is accompanied by XCI. The inactive X chromosome displays an atypical chromatin state, lacking DNA methylation and canonical heterochromatin marks. We demonstrate that extraembryonic differentiation and XCI are temporally linked. Using loss of function approaches, we found that XIST is required for XCI establishment in humans. Furthermore, we show that XCI is needed for the survival of human female extraembryonic cells. Together, these findings link XCI to the formation of human extraembryonic lineages, with important implications for human reproductive biology.

papers.abstract: Natural disasters can spark demands for democratic accountability yet impose losses and displacement that depress participation. We study approximately 16,000 Swedish tourists exposed to the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami who returned home to intact communities. Unlike most people exposed to natural disasters, they faced no increase in the cost of voting, so the case is well suited to studying motivational responses to disaster exposure. We link a survivor registry to population-wide administrative data (N up to 7 million) and use entropy balancing to compare survivors to matched non-exposed citizens over 25 years. Exposed individuals do not withdraw from participation. Their turnout is 1.4 percentage points higher in 2010 and 2018, a modest but persistent gap. The gap is more than twice as large among the bereaved. Mobilization is strongest among those exposed between ages 16 and 25, which is what habit formation would predict. A 2023 follow-up survey (3,956 respondents; N = 3198 to 3625 per analysis after item non-response) provides descriptive evidence that survivors still evaluate the government's crisis response negatively and have shifted their partisan sympathies away from the then-incumbent party. The findings indicate that failed crisis management may have lasting consequences for turnout and potentially party choice, and that the electoral stakes of disaster response extend beyond the disaster zone.

papers.abstract: Understanding rising atmospheric CO2 effects on the chemistry of the world's ecosystems remains nascent. CO2 dissolved in water forms carbonic acid, thereby lowering pH (ocean acidification [OA]). Diatoms, which generate 40% of ocean primary productivity, depend on dissolved silicon to construct their silica frustules; lower pH reduces silica (SiO2) solubility in seawater. Recent experiments document enhanced silica sedimentation under elevated CO2, implying reduced Si recycling and availability to support diatom production at the ecosystem scale. We tested this hypothesis using long-term data from a productive Pacific coastline undergoing rapid pH decline. Over two decades, as pH declined, dissolved Si:N and water column chlorophyll concurrently declined strongly. Accounting for variation in potential Si transport vectors did not change these relationships. Our results support the OA Si loss hypothesis and indicate that this process is already ongoing in some productive ocean regions, with implications for the carbon cycle, coastal food webs, and human well-being.

papers.abstract: While magnetometers based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond have emerged as the most important solid-state quantum sensors, ensembles are typically limited to a few percent optical contrast. Here, we demonstrate a laser threshold magnetometry-based NV system that achieves 100% optical contrast in combination with strong output signals up to 50 mW. By integrating the NV centers into a laser cavity, we show magnetic-field-dependent shifts of the laser threshold, allowing the laser system to be entirely switched off with the NV centers' magnetic resonance. We determine the photon-shot-noise fundamental sensitivity limit to be < 400 fT/ Hz for all vector components and demonstrate that it improves super-linearly with contrast. This sensitivity is not achieved at the usual cost of smaller linewidth, i.e., maintains good intrinsic dynamic range. This provides a perspective for highly sensitive magnetometry operated outside magnetically-shielded rooms for applications including magnetoencephalography, magnetic navigation, and magnetic anomaly detection.

papers.abstract: Tumor hypoxia has been recognized as a barrier to effective radiotherapy. Preclinical work identified the FDA approved smooth muscle relaxant papaverine (PPV) as having an "off target" activity as a mitochondrial inhibitor that reduces hypoxia and radiosensitizes model tumors. We conducted an IRB-approved phase 1 clinical trial to evaluate safety and feasibility of adding PPV to stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) for tumors of the lung. Eligible patients with early-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) or limited lung metastases who were candidates for SBRT (50 Gy in 4 or 5 fractions) were enrolled. Based on a Bayesian Optimal Interval (BOIN) design, patients were allocated to receive PPV 30-90 minutes prior to each SBRT fraction at 3 dose levels (DL): 0.5 mg/kg (DL-1), 1 mg/kg (DL1), or 2mg/kg (DL2). Nineteen patients enrolled and 18 completed study treatment and were evaluable, with a median follow up of 33.4 months. Among 18 evaluable patients, 7 had early-stage NSCLC, 2 had metastatic NSCLC, and 8 had lung metastases from other histologies. The maximum tolerated dose (MTD) was determined to be DL2, which had a dose limiting toxicity (DLT) rate posterior estimate of 0.17 (95% CI 0.01 to 0.53). The 2-year controls rates for local, regional and distant control were 100%, 94% and 82%, respectively. We demonstrate the feasibility and safety of PPV as a hypoxic radiosensitizer for SBRT. The MTD for this patient population is at least 2 mg/kg of PPV. Encouraging clinical results indicate that further investigation of PPV's utility as a tumor-selective radiosensitizer is warranted.

papers.abstract: Cardiac toxicity is a well-recognized, but poorly understood complication of radiotherapy (RT). In non-oncological settings, there is an established relationship between resting heart rate and cardiovascular health. To study the incidence and pattern of resting heart rate (rHR) as an early sign of cardiotoxicity among patients with non-metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treated with RT. We retrospectively analyzed serial rHR measurements of consecutive patients with locally advanced NSCLC treated with definitive chemoradiation (CRT) over 6-7 weeks of daily radiation treatments followed by immunotherapy (durvalumab) between 2017-2022. Radiation dose to the heart and 17 cardiac substructures were extracted. Associations between heart rate elevation, tachycardia, cardiac substructure dose and outcomes were evaluated using generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs) and regression analysis. We identified 110 patients, 56.4% with pre-existing heart disease. Median follow-up was 33.6 months. Median age was 70.4 years. Median rHR increased significantly during RT, rising from 81.5 bpm to 93 bpm at end of RT (p < 0.0001), remaining elevated in 30.6% of patients 12 months post-RT. Tachycardia incidence rose from 11.2% at baseline to 36.5% at 1-month post-RT (p < 0.0001). After adjusting for comorbidities, higher mean sinoatrial node (SAN) dose was associated with higher rHR elevation, delayed HR recovery and persistent tachycardia (all p < 0.05). Higher rHR during and after RT (β = 0.23, p = 0.005, and β = 13.49, p = 0.049, respectively), as well as the incidence of tachycardia episodes during RT were associated with increased odds of developing an arrhythmia (OR, 2.97, 95% CI, 1.17-7.52, p = 0.022). Elevated rHR and tachycardia are observed during and after RT for NSCLC and are associated with higher mean SAN dose. HR elevation was associated with increased risk of de novo arrhythmias, suggesting that heart rate may represent a non-invasive biomarker of subclinical cardiac injury. Prospective studies might be warranted to test the potential of routine HR monitoring and proactive dose reductions to the SAN to enable early detection and help mitigate the risk of post-treatment arrhythmia.

papers.abstract: Total mesorectal excision (TME) is standard for low rectal cancer (≤5cm from anal verge) but causes permanent stomas, functional impairments and surgical risks. Local excision (LE) suits early tumors (cTis-T1N0) but has higher recurrence in cT2+; watch-and-wait (WW) after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy risks residual disease. Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) improves outcomes, but prior LE trials had limitations. To evaluate TNT combined with planned LE for organ preservation in selected low rectal adenocarcinoma patients. Prospective single-arm phase 2 trial (June 2022-March 2024, tertiary center) enrolled 57/60 patients (cT1-3N0M0 nonmucinous adenocarcinoma, etc.). TNT: 50 Gy + 2 cycles of CapoX (standard capecitabine + oxaliplatin) + 4 consolidation CapoX. Clinical complete response (cCR)/near-complete clinical response (ncCR) patients had LE; others got TME. Patients with high-risk residual disease after LE also had additional TME. Median age was 61 years (28-79); 66.7% were male. cT3 tumors were present in 78.9%, and 78.9% had tumors ≤3 cm from the anal verge. After TNT, 47.4% achieved cCR and 38.6% achieved ncCR. Among surgically treated patients, the pathological complete response (pCR) rate was 68.6%; in the overall population, with WW counted as non-pCR, it was 61.4%. The total complete response rate, including pCR and cCR managed with WW, was 68.4%. Sphincter preservation was 94.7%. LE was associated with lower median blood loss (7 vs 50 mL; P<0.001) and shorter median hospitalization (7 vs 14 days; P=0.001) than TME. Grade 3 adverse events occurred in 22.8%, most commonly lymphocytopenia; no grade 4 or 5 events occurred. Low anterior resection syndrome (LARS) scores were assessed after TNT and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively. At 6 months, LARS outcomes favored LE (80.0% vs 53.8% reporting no LARS; P=0.027). Wexner incontinence scores did not differ significantly between groups at any time point. TNT with planned LE is feasible in cT1-3N0M0 low rectal cancer, yielding a pCR rate of 61.4% in the overall population, 94.7% sphincter preservation, and acceptable toxicity. However, the non-randomized design and immature 3-year organ-preservation endpoint limit this study to a feasibility assessment and do not permit conclusions regarding comparative effectiveness versus WW. papers.abstract: This Special Report analyzes current radiotherapy data standards, determines which radiotherapy data elements should propagate between them, and identifies the barriers to that propagation to improve interoperability and data utilization in clinical care and research. We compared five data standards-OMOP, CDISC SDTM, FHIR, NAACCR, and the Operational Ontology for Oncology (O3)-and one ontology framework, the OBO Foundry, for radiotherapy data representation, strengths, limitations, and implementation maturity, and examined harmonization initiatives including NRG's O3-based conversion frameworks, CodeX mCODE, and ESTRO and IAEA efforts. We then scored a 90-item benchmark drawn from radiotherapy operational and trial-reporting requirements, partitioned the radiotherapy items by whether and where they should propagate, and matched each barrier to a remediation route and owning body. Counting only unqualified matches, O3 covered 46 of 62 radiotherapy-specific items (74%) versus 15 (24%) for OMOP, 12 (19%) for NAACCR, 11 (18%) for FHIR, and none for OBO Foundry; on the 28 general clinical items the ordering reversed (OMOP 79%, FHIR 71%, NAACCR 46%, O3 25%, OBO Foundry 4%). Each standard is strongest on the items its target function was built to serve. Wholesale propagation is therefore unwarranted: 20 course-summary elements should converge across standards, 26 planning and adaptive elements warrant selective adoption, and 16 voxel- and machine-level artifacts should be referenced by DICOM unique identifier rather than replicated. Harmonization requires ontology-driven approaches using O3 as the semantic backbone with mappings to FHIR, OMOP and CDISC, applied to a defined tier of elements rather than the full element set. The principal barriers are process barriers-structural, terminological, burden-related and tooling-related-each with a named owner and an existing route. Standardized formats alone are insufficient; they require robust information systems, validation, and governance. Harmonization improves real-world data utility but cannot resolve biases inherent to nonrandomized data. Coordinated international collaboration remains critical for advancing precision radiation oncology.

papers.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is characterized by chronic hemolytic anemia and a propensity to acute exacerbations such as post-transfusion hyperhemolysis syndrome (HHS). While erythrocyte injury is secondary to hemoglobin S polymerization, the underlying pathophysiologic driver, the mechanism by which sickle erythrocytes are then removed from circulation is largely regulated by the immune system. Multiple pathways potentially play a role, driven by pathological changes within both the cellular and humoral immune system. The review examines what is known regarding changes to the outer membrane of the sickle erythrocyte (including the expression of phosphatidylserine (PS), mannose, CD47 and CD95/Fas), the role of plasma-derived opsonins (including Gas6, MFG-E8, Protein S, MBL, TSP1, IgG and C3b) and the macrophage receptors that recognize and bind these molecules (including TREM2, TIM4, MerTK, integrins αvβ3/5, CD206, CD209/DC-SIGN, SIRPα, FasL, FcR, and CR). Drawing upon the results of investigations by our group and others, we conclude with a proposed model for clearance of erythrocytes in SCD, in which chronic hemolysis predominantly occurs through extravascular erythrophagocytosis, whereas acute hemolytic events involve a shift towards intravascular hemolysis via complement assembly into the membrane attack complex, Fas-mediated erythronecroptosis, and heme-mediated ferroptosis. The process by which transfusion may accelerate these pathways and induce HHS is also considered.

papers.abstract: Emicizumab has transformed hemophilia A (HA) management by enabling effective subcutaneous prophylaxis independent of inhibitor status. However, its constitutive activity and lack of sensitivity to anticoagulant feedback contribute to excessive thrombin generation under certain conditions, particularly when combined with bypassing agents, a liability increasingly recognized as a class effect of FVIII-mimetic antibodies. We engineered an "AutoRegulated" (AR) FVIII-mimetic antibody by integrating a short thrombin cleavable peptide sensitive to the proteolytic activity of thrombin in the hinge region of both emicizumab arms. Insertion of the peptide did not impair structural integrity and biological function with AR-emicizumab demonstrating EC50 values of FVIII-mimetic activity and correction of blood loss in HA mice comparable to the parental emicizumab. However, the presence of thrombin-mediated AR enabled thrombin-responsive proteolytic inactivation upon exposure to supra-physiological thrombin levels, whereas the parental emicizumab remained unaffected. The dynamic control provided by AR efficiently reduced the procoagulant effects induced by co-administration of activated Prothrombin Complex Concentrates (aPCC). In thrombin generation assays, AR-emicizumab significantly attenuated the excessive thrombin peak observed with emicizumab. Similarly, in vivo, the presence of thrombin-mediated AR prevented platelet consumptive coagulopathy and reduced the microvascular pulmonary thrombosis induced by the parental molecule without affecting the systemic levels of the therapeutic antibody. This on-demand self-limiting mechanism aligns therapeutic activity with local hemostatic needs, may offer a promising therapeutic approach for HA patients, while establishing a generalizable strategy to improve the safety profile of next-generation hemostatic biologics.

papers.abstract: Positive margins after breast-conserving surgery (BCS) require additional surgery, a negative patient experience that also adds costs to care. Pilot trials indicate the Breast Cancer LocatorTM (BCL), a novel supine magnetic resonance imaging-based guidance system, helps surgeons resect cancers with a low positive margin rate (PMR). Our objective was to evaluate BCL noninferiority and superiority compared with wire localization (WL) in reducing the PMR with BCS. Patients with nonpalpable, magnetic resonance imaging-visualized invasive breast cancer or ductal carcinoma in situ undergoing BCS were prospectively randomized to either BCL or WL. In total, 418 randomized patients underwent surgery. The PMR was 14.4% (30/209) in the BCL group and 21.1% (44/209) in the WL group, a relative decrease of 32%. In primary analysis, the treatment difference was -7.1% (95.4% confidence interval [CI] -14.3 to 0.1). Noninferiority was demonstrated (p = 0.011). The one-sided p-value for superiority (p = 0.025) slightly exceeded the prespecified significance level of 0.023. In prespecified analysis stratified by final tumor type, the PMR was significantly lower in the BCL group (p = 0.019). Fewer BCL patients underwent re-excision: 12.9% versus 19.6%, a relative decrease of 34%. The PMR for all tumor types was lower in the BCL group, with a > 60% relative reduction in PMR in patients with ductal carcinoma in situ (20.6% vs. 53.3% [95% CI -52.1 to -9.1]) and invasive lobular carcinoma (9.1% vs. 25.6% [95% CI -32.9 to -0.2]). Adverse event rates were similar. BCL was noninferior to WL and superior in analysis stratified by final tumor type. Clinically meaningful relative reductions in PMR and re-excision rates were observed.

papers.abstract: In proliferative glioblastoma, a subset of tumor cells survives early temozolomide (TMZ) exposure and drives eventual-resistance, yet the underlying mechanism remains unclear. We found that MYC target activation was associated with attenuated TMZ survival benefit in CGGA cohorts. In patient-derived MYC-high glioma cells, TMZ increased apoptosis but left a larger residual viable population due to enhanced proliferation; we defined these surviving cells as pioneer resistant (P-R) cells, which exhibited reduced TMZ sensitivity and a competitive survival advantage. Mechanistically, P-R cells adopted a senescence-like state via two coordinated arms of chromatin remodeling. On one hand, H3K27ac-dependent super-enhancers were gained at senescence-associated secretory genes; the CBP/p300 inhibitor A485 reverted the senescence-like state and restored TMZ cytotoxicity; On another hand, chromatin closed, reducing MYC occupancy at cell-cycle genes despite unchanged MYC protein, and suppressed nascent transcription and m6A modification, accompanied by cell-cycle arrest in some P-R cells. Furthermore, time-course analysis revealed that chromatin closure at cell-cycle genes is likely a temporally ordered epigenetic remodeling process, initiated by DNA damage-associated G2/M arrest mediated by WEE1 activation, followed by γH2AX-mediated recruitment of SUV39H1, which deposits H3K9me3 at MYC-bound loci to close chromatin. Functionally, early, but not delayed, inhibition of WEE1 with the novel brain-penetrant inhibitor TSL2304 blocked senescence-like epigenetic reprogramming, synergized with TMZ in vitro, and significantly prolonged survival in an orthotopic glioblastoma model. Together, these findings reveal a temporally ordered epigenetic remodeling in MYC-high glioblastoma that promotes survival after early TMZ exposure, and identify early WEE1 inhibition as a strategy to synergize with TMZ.

papers.abstract: Direct RAS targeting has progressed from pharmacologic proof of concept to routine treatment for selected KRAS G12C-mutant cancers. KRAS G12C inhibitors and KRAS G12C-EGFR combinations established allele- and lineage-specific treatment paradigms. More recently, the multiselective RAS(ON) inhibitor daraxonrasib became the first FDA-approved direct RAS-targeted therapy for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, while the KRAS G12D-directed degrader setidegrasib remains investigational. Target engagement alone, however, does not ensure durable disease control, and the same drug class can perform differently across tumor lineages. This Review develops an adaptive RAS signaling ecosystem model in which allele and isoform biology, membrane organization, feedback architecture, mutant-wild-type RAS crosstalk, co-mutation patterns, chromatin state, epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity, metabolism, spatial heterogeneity, the tumor microenvironment and treatment delivery jointly determine pathway dependence and therapeutic escape. Comparisons among pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, colorectal cancer, lung adenocarcinoma and NRAS-mutant melanoma show how related oncogenic RAS nodes acquire different vulnerabilities in distinct tissue contexts. We integrate direct RAS inhibition with mechanism-guided vertical and horizontal strategies directed at feedback rebound, bypass signaling, cell-state persistence, stromal protection, metabolic adaptation and immune exclusion. We then translate this model into a biomarker-integrated development framework that links serial circulating tumor DNA, modality-matched pharmacodynamic assays, paired tissue sampling, spatial profiling and toxicity-aware scheduling to prespecified, falsifiable treatment hypotheses. RAS dependence is conditional rather than absolute. Durable control will require strategies that match the RAS allele and tumor lineage to the dominant adaptive circuitry, verify that target and pathway suppression persist over time, and maintain sufficient dose intensity to exert biologically effective pressure without disabling antitumor immunity or normal-tissue function.

papers.abstract: T cells recognize antigens from pathogens and transformed cells. Yet what antigen is "ideal"? We propose a theoretical framework in which recognition is governed by T cell selection maximized near, not far from, self. Genomic errors generate antigens closer to self that paradoxically overlap with pathogen antigens and are immunogenic and non-self. We formalize this concept as the Neoantigen Quality Model, recasting antigen recognition as an adaptation to surveil the self and non-self living worlds.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) ranks among the deadliest malignancies, with limited survival benefits despite recent therapeutic advances. Few prognostic biomarkers are available for PDAC monitoring in clinical practice. We conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate and synthesise evidence on the prognostic significance of miRNA expression in PDAC. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42023463542). We conducted a systematic search in PubMed, CENTRAL, and Embase on January 27, 2026, to identify studies assessing miRNA expression levels in patients with PDAC with reported overall survival (OS) or progression-free survival (PFS) outcomes. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model. Prediction intervals (PI) were reported if feasible. Separate analyses were performed by miRNA functional categories: oncogenic, tumour suppressor, chemoresistance-related, metastasis-related, and dual-role miRNAs. A total of 142 studies, including 13,824 patients, were included. High expression of oncogenic miRNAs was associated with worse univariate OS (HR 1.70, 95% CI 1.38-2.10; 95% PI 0.63-4.57) and PFS (HR 2.25, 95% CI 1.63-3.10; 95% PI 1.11-4.55). High expression of chemoresistance-related miRNAs was associated with worse multivariate OS (HR 2.11, 95% CI 1.68-2.66; 95% PI 0.96-4.68) and PFS (HR 2.51, 95% CI 1.89-3.33; 95% PI 1.58-3.97). Between-study heterogeneity varied substantially across pooled analyses (I2 range 0-94%). miRNA-21 was the most frequently studied individual biomarker and showed a consistent association with worse multivariate OS (HR 2.24, 95% CI 1.95-2.57; 95% PI 1.92-2.61). Elevated expression of oncogenic and chemoresistance-related miRNAs is associated with worse survival outcomes in PDAC. However, substantial heterogeneity and wide prediction intervals observed in several pooled analyses indicate variability in effect sizes across studies. Among the investigated biomarkers, miRNA-21 has shown the most consistent prognostic association and may represent the strongest candidate for future clinical implementation. Further validation and standardisation are required before miRNA profiling can be integrated into routine clinical practice. None to declare.
